about: MUTATING (creates only its own scratch objects, and removes them only on its own failure; READ-ONLY to the system of record) — STARTS the restore drill before the Postgres move (backlog 156eb6e5; design 3c475a19 car 4's risk section: 'A backup nobody has restored is a belief') and RETURNS; read-restore-drill reads it. Asked for by David on 2026-11-14 ~15:40Z ('file both cars and target 19:30Z'), the move's precondition. Split in two by backlog a1cbd16c after the first real run, ops-request 24fd49e7, waited 47 minutes on the Job inside the forge's single ops-runner lane (alarm 58c101a7), failed on its 2700 s DeadlineExceeded, and lost the restore log with the pod the Job controller deleted. Takes no arguments. Through the forge's ops_kubectl door it creates ONE Job, boss/boss-restore-drill, from this checkout's infra/forge/restore-drill-job.yaml (the forge registry host filled in, nothing else), and one ConfigMap of the same name owned by that Job carrying infra/forge/gcs-readback.py and infra/forge/restore-drill-pod.sh. The pod is pinned by nodeSelector boss.dev/purpose=database (w-3, the estate registry's data node) and its scratch claim is a generic ephemeral volume of StorageClass longhorn-restore-drill (one replica, diskSelector postgres: Longhorn disk u-postgres), made for the pod and deleted with it. Its fetch initContainer is gcs-readback.py, check-gcs-backup's own newest-archive selection and validation (every objects.list page, newest exact boss-<stamp>.sql.gz by creation instant, pinned generation, sha256, gzip -t, pg_dump's completion trailer), keeping exactly the bytes it verified; the Secret boss/boss-gcs-offsite is MOUNTED into that container 0400 as the nightly uploader mounts it, so this host never reads its value. Its restore container initdb's a fresh postgres 16 in the dump's own image on the claim (unix socket only), creates the live role names NOLOGIN, restores the dump with ON_ERROR_STOP while printing a progress line every 60 s (elapsed seconds, the scratch database's pg_database_size, the statement psql is running), ENDS ITSELF at its inner deadline (DRILL_RESTORE_DEADLINE_S, 14400 s, in the manifest) so a slow restore leaves a Failed pod with its log, and reads count(*) of audit_log, jobs and steps and max(audit_log.id) there, then the same four from the LIVE system of record and whether the live log holds the dump's newest audit id — every live session READ-ONLY twice (PGOPTIONS default_transaction_read_only=on and SET default_transaction_read_only = on, the switch-instance-database shape), its URL from Secret boss-secrets database-url as an environment variable and never printed. The Job's activeDeadlineSeconds (18000 s) is only the backstop above the inner deadline, and the script refuses a manifest where it is not above it. It never execs into, mounts or writes the live database, its volume or its Pod. THE BOUNDS refuse before any create (exit 78): the StorageClass is the tree's; exactly one Node carries boss.dev/purpose=database, uncordoned and untainted, and its Longhorn node has a schedulable disk at /var/mnt/postgres tagged postgres; both Secrets exist (read by name only); and NO drill stands — a running one is never touched, and a FINISHED one is not removed here, because its log is the record: the refusal names read-restore-drill, which records it and then removes it. IT REMOVES ONLY WHAT IT MADE, and only when it fails after the create (a refused ConfigMap, a Job that does not read back): the Job by its uid (DeleteOptions preconditions.uid, Foreground), an EXIT trap covering the runner's TERM, the claim and the ConfigMap going with it by garbage collection. THE EFFECT is the line printed after the Job reads back by its uid: STARTED, the uid, its creation time, both deadlines and the time it ends by at the latest, and the exact follow-up, 'boss ops forge read-restore-drill --wait'. No clock rule files that read: the start's answer names it, and the Job's ttlSecondsAfterFinished (a day) keeps a finished drill for it. NO PASSKEY, for registry-probe's and prove-gate-volume's reasons: no packet-supplied word at all; one bounded create of the tree's own Job and its own ConfigMap; it adds no capability — the nightly boss-pg-backup CronJob already mounts both Secrets in this namespace unattended and reads the whole live database with pg_dump, and check-gcs-backup reads the same archive weekly; and a plan would render nothing an approver could judge. TIMEOUT 300, inside the forge queue's 5-minute bound: the door's first-time image pull (120 s), a dozen kubectl reads bounded at 20 s, two creates at 30 s and one read-back; it waits on nothing the drill does. Pinned by crates/core/boss-testing/tests/drill_gcs_restore_sh.rs.
effect: ^drill-gcs-restore: STARTED Job [a-z-]+/[a-z-]+ \(uid [^ )]+\) at [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}[Z] — the restore ends itself at its inner deadline of [0-9]+s and the Job's backstop deadline of [0-9]+s ends it by [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}[Z] at the latest; nothing waits on it here[.] Read its progress or its verdict with: boss ops forge read-restore-drill --wait \(it removes nothing while the drill runs\)$
